### 1. Representative Fraction (R.F.)
$$\text{R.F.} = \frac{\text{Length on Map}}{\text{Actual Distance}} = \frac{5\text{ cm}}{10\text{ km}} = \frac{5\text{ cm}}{10 \times 10^5\text{ cm}} = \frac{1}{200,000}$$

### 2. Length of Scale
$$\text{Length of Scale} = \text{R.F.} \times \text{Maximum Distance} = \frac{1}{200,000} \times 30\text{ km} = \frac{30 \times 10^5\text{ cm}}{200,000} = 15\text{ cm}$$

### 3. Construction of Plain Scale
* Draw a straight line of length $15\text{ cm}$.
* Divide this line into $3$ equal parts, each representing $10\text{ km}$.
* Subdivide the first part on the left into $10$ equal divisions, where each division represents $1\text{ km}$ (Least Count = $1\text{ km}$).
* Mark the divisions $0, 10, 20$ to the right and units $1, 2, ... 10$ to the left from the zero mark.

### 4. Marking $17\text{ km}$
* Take the main division mark for $10\text{ km}$ to the right of zero, and count $7$ subdivisions to the right (or use the zero-mark combining $10$ on right and $7$ on left depending on scale layout) to precisely indicate $17\text{ km}$.
proTip: Always compute the length of the scale first before drawing to ensure it fits neatly within the drawing sheet layout limits (typically 15 cm to 18 cm).
